slides.title: Five things people still get wrong about perimenopause
"You're too young."
slides.body: Menopause usually happens between 45 and 55, but it can happen earlier. Perimenopause, the years of change before it, starts earlier still.

slides.title: "It's just hot flushes."
slides.body: The NHS lists low mood, anxiety, memory problems, joint pain, headaches, itchy skin and more.

slides.title: "It's over in a year."
slides.body: Symptoms usually last 7 to 9 years, sometimes longer, and they can change along the way.

slides.title: "You'll need a blood test."
slides.body: There's no routine test. For women over 45 with symptoms, NICE says it can be diagnosed without one.

slides.title: "There's nothing you can do."
slides.body: There are things you can try at home, and treatments a GP can talk through with you.
